description: CALL <proc>(name => value) - Snowflake NAMED ARGUMENTS. A named argument binds to the parameter whose name it MATCHES, so order is free and a DEFAULTED parameter may be skipped entirely. A CALL's arguments are all-named or all-positional: mixing them fails 'illegal mixing of named and positional arguments for function P_AB', live-verified, and the restriction is CALL's alone - the same mixed shape on a UDF works there. Exercised for the top-level CALL, the var := (CALL ...) assignment form, and a bare CALL inside a procedure body. An unknown argument name is rejected. Converted 1:1 from scripting/CallNamedArgumentsTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE p_ab(a INT, b INT) RETURNS INT LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN RETURN :a * 10 + :b; END $$

error.messageContains: illegal mixing of named and positional arguments

steps.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE p_def(a INT, b INT DEFAULT 5) RETURNS INT LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN RETURN :a * 10 + :b; END $$
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE p_ab(a INT, b INT) RETURNS INT LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN RETURN :a * 10 + :b; END $$
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE p_assign() RETURNS INT LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ DECLARE r INT; BEGIN r := (CALL p_ab(b => 2, a => 1)); RETURN r; END $$
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE p_ins(v INT) RETURNS INT LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN INSERT INTO call_log VALUES (:v); RETURN 1; END $$
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE p_caller() RETURNS INT LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN CALL p_ins(v => 77); RETURN 0; END $$
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE p_ab(a INT, b INT) RETURNS INT LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN RETURN :a * 10 + :b; END $$
